column1: extremity§Cold reaches the extremities first, which is why gloves matter.§寒冷最先侵袭**四肢末端**，所以手套很重要。
extroverted§An extroverted teacher can drown a quiet class.§**外向**的老师可能把一个安静的班级淹没。
exuberant§Her exuberant marginal notes are half the value of the book.§她在页边写下的**活泼**批注占了这本书一半的价值。
exultant§An exultant tone in a report is usually premature.§报告里的**欢欣**语气通常为时过早。
exultation§Exultation lasted a day; the paperwork lasted a year.§**欢欣**持续了一天，文书工作持续了一年。
fabricate§The workshop fabricates parts no supplier still makes.§这个作坊**制造**着已无供应商生产的零件。
fabrication§Steel fabrication moved out of the city in the 1970s.§钢结构**制造**业在七十年代迁出了城市。
facetious§Being facetious about a deadline does not move it.§拿截止日期**开玩笑**并不能让它挪动。
facile§A facile fluency in three languages is not the same as depth.§三种语言的**浅易流利**与深度不是一回事。
faintly§She smiled faintly and changed the subject.§她**淡淡一笑**，转开了话题。
fallacious§The reasoning is fallacious in a way that is hard to see quickly.§这个推理的**谬误**之处不容易一眼看出。
famish§Famished after eight hours, they ate standing up.§八小时后**饿坏**了，他们站着就吃了起来。
fanfare§A short fanfare preceded every announcement on the hour.§每逢整点的通告前都有一小段**号角声**。
fastidious§He is fastidious about tools and careless about time.§他对工具**一丝不苟**，对时间却随意。
fathom§The lead line showed twelve fathoms and dropping.§测深绳显示十二**英寻**，还在变浅。
felicitous§Not every accident is felicitous, but this one was.§并非每次意外都**恰到好处**，但这一次是。
feral§A feral cat kept the granary free of mice for years.§一只**野猫**多年来让粮仓不见老鼠。
fertilize§Only one flower in twenty gets fertilized in a cold spring.§寒冷的春天里，二十朵花里只有一朵能**受精**。
fervent§His fervent letters arrived weekly for two years.§他**热切**的信件持续两年每周一封。
feverish§A feverish market corrects itself, usually badly.§**狂热**的市场会自我修正，通常修正得很难看。
fickle§Fashion is fickle and the archive is patient.§时尚**变幻无常**，档案却有耐心。
fictional§The names are fictional and the streets are real.§名字是**虚构的**，街道是真实的。
fidelity§Fidelity to the source sometimes produces an ugly sentence.§**忠于原文**有时会造出难看的句子。
figurative§Read it in the figurative sense and the paragraph works.§按**比喻**义来读，这一段就通了。
filial§Filial piety is a translation that loses most of the word.§“**filial piety**”这个译法丢掉了原词的大部分含义。
finagle§She finagled a week's extension out of a very firm editor.§她从一位极其严格的编辑那里**哄到**了一周宽限。
finesse§It took finesse to correct him without an audience noticing.§要在不被观众察觉的情况下纠正他，需要**技巧**。
fiscal§Fiscal caution in good years is what makes bad years survivable.§好年头的**财政**谨慎，让坏年头得以熬过。
fitful§Progress was fitful and, over ten years, considerable.§进展**断断续续**，十年下来却很可观。
flabbergast§He was flabbergasted to find his own name in the index.§在索引里看到自己的名字，他**大吃一惊**。
flagrant§A flagrant foul in the last minute decided the match.§最后一分钟一次**明显的犯规**决定了比赛。
flamboyance§Flamboyance in the margins, austerity in the text.§页边**花哨**，正文却极简。
flank§Two officers were sent to protect the flank.§两名军官被派去掩护**侧翼**。
flatter§The photograph flatters the building and lies about the street.§这张照片**美化**了建筑，也在街道上撒了谎。
flaunt§The house flaunts its age and hides its repairs.§这栋房子**炫耀**自己的年岁，掩藏自己的修补。
flaw§The flaw in the argument is a missing decade.§这个论证的**破绽**是缺了十年。
flimsy§Flimsy paper survived because nobody thought it worth reusing.§这种**薄纸**之所以留存下来，是因为没人觉得值得再利用。
flippant§He is flippant in public and meticulous on the page.§他在公开场合**轻佻**，落到纸上却一丝不苟。
flora§Alpine flora begins abruptly at about eighteen hundred metres.§高山**植物群**在大约一千八百米处骤然开始。
florid§His face turned florid and he sat down without finishing.§他脸**涨得通红**，没说完就坐下了。
floridity§A little floridity suits the subject; a page of it does not.§少许**华丽**适合这个题材，整页就不行了。
flotilla§A fishing flotilla of thirty boats left before dawn.§三十条船的**渔船队**在天亮前出发。
flotsam§The beach collects flotsam from four countries.§这片海滩上聚集着四个国家的**漂浮物**。
flounder§The company floundered for a year and then found its market.§这家公司**挣扎**了一年，随后找到了自己的市场。
foible§Every good editor tolerates one foible in a good writer.§每位好编辑都会容忍好作者的一个**小毛病**。
foil§Gold foil a fraction of a millimetre thick covers the whole dome.§不到一毫米厚的**金箔**覆盖了整个穹顶。
fondness§There is a fondness in the way he describes the machinery.§他描述那些机器时带着一种**喜爱**。
foolhardy§Foolhardy is what we call brave when it fails.§我们把失败了的勇敢叫作**有勇无谋**。
forage§They foraged for two days and found one edible root.§他们**找了两天食物**，只找到一种可食的根。
forbearance§Forbearance is not the same as approval.§**忍让**并不等于赞同。
forego§Nothing in the rules requires you to forego a second attempt.§规则里没有任何条款要求你**放弃**第二次尝试。
forerunner§A forerunner is only recognized after the successor arrives.§**先驱**只有在后继者出现之后才被承认。
foreshadow§Nothing in the diary foreshadows what happened that March.§日记里没有任何内容**预示**三月发生的事。
foresight§Foresight is cheap in retrospect and rare in advance.§事后看**远见**很廉价，事前它却很稀有。
forestall§A short note forestalled a very long argument.§一张短笺**预先化解**了一场很长的争论。
forfeit§By missing the deadline he forfeited the only advantage he had.§错过截止日期，他**丧失**了自己唯一的优势。
forgettable§A forgettable title has sunk more good books than bad reviews.§**过目即忘**的书名毁掉的好书比差评还多。
forgivable§The error is forgivable; repeating it in the reprint is not.§这个错误**可以原谅**，重印时再犯就不能了。
forgo§To forgo the footnotes is to forgo the argument.§**放弃**脚注就等于放弃论证。
formality§Formality in a letter can be a way of keeping distance.§信中的**客套**可能是一种保持距离的方式。
formidable§The formidable part of the walk is the last kilometre.§这段路最**艰难的**是最后一公里。
formulaic§Formulaic writing is easy to produce and easy to skip.§**套路化**的文字容易写，也容易被跳过。
formulate§Formulate the objection before you decide whether it is fatal.§先把反对意见**表述**清楚，再判断它是否致命。
forsake§The birds forsake the cliff by the second week of August.§到八月第二周，鸟群就**离开**了这片崖壁。
fortify§Coffee fortified them through a very long committee meeting.§咖啡**支撑**他们熬过了一场极长的委员会会议。
fortuitous§A fortuitous misprint gave the journal its name.§一次**偶然**的印刷错误给了这份期刊它的名字。
founder§The founder's portrait hangs where nobody has to look at it.§**创办人**的画像挂在没人非看不可的地方。
fragility§Fragility is why the best copies are the least read.§正因为**脆弱**，最好的本子才最少被翻阅。
